description: Guide the student to collect realtime market updates from a streaming or polling endpoint, store timestamped updates as a CSV file, and teach quant microstructure and data-quality concepts.
student_opening: My professor asked us to collect realtime market updates from a streaming or polling endpoint. I'm new to both Python and finance — can you start from the basics?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Tutor guides the student to build a realtime data capture pipeline, save timestamped market updates to CSV, explain trade-vs-quote semantics and bid-ask spread context, and address latency, out-of-order tick, and timezone/session handling risks.
required_capabilities: Capture realtime market updates and store them as timestamped CSV
Explain quote vs trade semantics and bid-ask spread context
Handle latency, out-of-order ticks, and session/timezone boundaries
Apply practical quality checks for realtime data streams
ground_truth.termination_criteria: (1) Showed actual code that captures realtime or simulated market updates from a streaming or polling endpoint and saves timestamped records as a CSV file in the workspace. (2) Explained concrete microstructure concepts using evidence from the captured data, such as trade-vs-quote semantics, bid-ask spread interpretation, or timestamp ordering issues. (3) Responded to a student follow-up with one additional concrete quality check or latency diagnostic on the captured stream, such as out-of-order detection, gap analysis, or session boundary handling. Once all 3 steps have been computationally demonstrated, the session is complete.
